Lets you set a custom user agent that the headless Chrome browser assumes.

## CLI flag

Use `--user-agent` with the following commands. Follow a command link for its syntax and examples.

| Command                                                         | Flag                   |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| [`remotion studio`](/docs/cli/studio)                           | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion render`](/docs/cli/render)                           | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion still`](/docs/cli/still)                             | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion compositions`](/docs/cli/compositions)               | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion benchmark`](/docs/cli/benchmark)                     | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion gpu`](/docs/cli/gpu)                                 | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion lambda render`](/docs/lambda/cli/render)             | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion lambda still`](/docs/lambda/cli/still)               | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion lambda compositions`](/docs/lambda/cli/compositions) | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion cloudrun render`](/docs/cloudrun/cli/render)         | `--user-agent <value>` |
| [`remotion cloudrun still`](/docs/cloudrun/cli/still)           | `--user-agent <value>` |

## APIs that have this option

The following APIs accept this option:

- [`getCompositionsOnLambda()`](/docs/lambda/getcompositionsonlambda#useragent)
- [`renderStillOnLambda()`](/docs/lambda/renderstillonlambda#useragent)
- [`renderFrames()`](/docs/renderer/render-frames#useragent)
- [`renderMedia()`](/docs/renderer/render-media#useragent)
- [`renderStill()`](/docs/renderer/render-still#useragent)
